# available read concern — facts

> Source-anchored units about available read concern: 14 across 6 sources. Each line ends in the URL and anchor it came from; `keywords:` names the lexicon terms that matched.

## How-to and procedures

- [statement] The client URI option readConcernLevel defines the level for the read concern, and read preference is a separate setting that describes how clients route reads to replica set members. Read concern is specified as readConcern: { level: ... }, and "available" is a supported level. Sources: https://github.com/mongodb/specifications/blob/master/source/read-write-concern/read-write-concern.md ; https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/read-preference.md — https://github.com/mongodb/specifications/blob/master/source/read-write-concern/read-write-concern.md · keywords: available read concern · also: https://github.com/mongodb/specifications/blob/master/source/uri-options/uri-options.md

## Problems, failure modes and limitations

- [statement] "available" cannot be used with causally consistent sessions or transactions. (high confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/read-concern-available.md · keywords: available read concern · also: https://github.com/mongodb/mongo/blob/master/src/mongo/db/repl/README.md

## Comparisons and alternatives

- [statement] MongoDB documentation lists local as the default for reads against both primaries and secondaries. Treat available as an explicit choice rather than assuming secondary reads select it. Deployment or client settings can override defaults. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-20) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/mongodb-defaults/ · keywords: available read concern

## Facts and statements

- [statement] Read concern "available" returns data from the serving instance without guaranteeing majority replication; returned data may subsequently be rolled back. (high confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/read-concern-available.md · keywords: available read concern · also: https://www.alibabacloud.com/help/en/mongodb/use-cases/transactions-and-read-write-concern
- [statement] For sharded collections, "available" does not require a check that the correct shard received the query and, unlike "local", does not contact the shard's primary or the config servers for updated metadata. This gives greater tolerance for partitions but can return orphaned documents if the shard is undergoing chunk migration. Sources: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/read-concern-available.md ; https://www.php.net/mongodb-driver-readconcern — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/read-concern-available.md · keywords: available read concern · also: https://github.com/mongodb/mongo/blob/master/src/mongo/db/repl/README.md, https://www.alibabacloud.com/help/en/mongodb/use-cases/transactions-and-read-write-concern
- [statement] For unsharded collections, including standalone and replica set deployments, "available" and "local" behave identically. Choosing "available" alone therefore adds no distinct unsharded read semantics to an Atlas deployment. (high confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/read-concern-available.md · keywords: available read concern · also: https://github.com/mongodb/mongo/blob/master/src/mongo/db/repl/README.md
- [statement] The performance benefit is conditional: implementation notes describe potentially faster reads by avoiding metadata-refresh communication, not a quantified cross-cloud latency improvement or an unconditional ability to serve every read during a partition. (high confidence) — https://github.com/mongodb/mongo/blob/master/src/mongo/db/repl/README.md · keywords: available read concern · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/read-concern-available.md
- [statement] SERVER-69219 documents using "available" to find unowned documents, but a shard-key equality predicate can target only some shards and miss unowned documents elsewhere. The issue describes an aggregation with {$replaceWith: "$$ROOT"} as a workaround; this is historical troubleshooting evidence, not a verified recipe for every current server release. (low confidence) — https://jira.mongodb.org/browse/SERVER-69219 · keywords: available read concern
- [statement] The 2019 MongoDB-authored paper Tunable Consistency in MongoDB (Schultz, Avitabile, Cabral, VLDB 2019) states that it does not discuss sharding at all, so its coverage of the "available" read concern (mentioned only briefly alongside "snapshot" and causal consistency) says nothing about sharded behavior; its consistency discussion should not be treated as validation of this level in sharded deployments. Sources: https://hn.jakechampion.name/reader/http://muratbuffalo.blogspot.com/2024/02/tunable-consistency-in-mongodb.html — https://www.vldb.org/pvldb/vol12/p2071-schultz.pdf · keywords: available read concern
- [statement] ApsaraDB for MongoDB documentation dated June 2, 2026 calls "available" the default for reads against secondaries in a sharded cluster. Current MongoDB default-setting documentation lists "local" for secondary reads, so the ApsaraDB-specific statement should not be generalized into an Atlas default. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-06-02) Sources: https://www.alibabacloud.com/help/en/mongodb/use-cases/transactions-and-read-write-concern ; https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/mongodb-defaults.md — https://www.alibabacloud.com/help/en/mongodb/use-cases/transactions-and-read-write-concern · keywords: available read concern · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/mongodb-defaults/
- [statement] For sharded clusters, read concern "available" provides greater tolerance for partitions: queries do not require a check that the correct shard received them and, unlike "local", do not contact the shard's primary or the config servers for updated metadata. The trade-off is that queries may return orphaned documents during chunk migration, and the receiving shard may not be the authoritative owner of the requested data. Sources: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/read-concern-available.md ; https://www.php.net/mongodb-driver-readconcern — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/read-concern-available.md · keywords: available read concern · also: https://github.com/mongodb/mongo/blob/master/src/mongo/db/repl/README.md
- [statement] Reading the newest data present on one node does not establish that it is the newest data in the system; available provides no guarantee of globally fresh results. (high confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/read-concern-available.md · keywords: available read concern · also: https://www.alibabacloud.com/help/en/mongodb/use-cases/transactions-and-read-write-concern
- [statement] Mongoose Query.readConcern('available') sets the query read concern; Query.readConcern('a') is its documented alias. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-20) — https://mongoosejs.com/docs/api/query.html · keywords: available read concern
- [statement] For Atlas Multi-Cloud applications, using available as an availability optimization requires accepting rollback and, for sharded collections, ownership-related anomalies. This is an application-design inference from server semantics, not an Atlas-specific failover or latency guarantee. (medium confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/read-concern-available.md · keywords: available read concern · also: https://github.com/mongodb/mongo/blob/master/src/mongo/db/repl/README.md
